findings.title: Error-focus gate is a substring match on the raw request query
findings.body: `"event.type:error" in query` is True for `!event.type:error` (exclude errors) and for `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. In both cases `count()` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()` (sum of sample_weight) even though transaction rows are in scope and carry no sample weight, so counts come out wrong or the query fails. The gate also reads `request.GET['query']` (line 135) rather than the query string that actually executes. The split paths in organization_events_stats.py append `AND !event.type:transaction` or `AND event.type:transaction` to the query, so the gate's decision and the executed query can disagree.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses the request's dataset instead of the dataset the call runs against
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(...) receives `dataset`, the closed-over variable from get(), not `scoped_dataset`, which is the parameter this _get_event_stats call actually runs on. The dashboard split path calls _get_event_stats with `discover` for errors_only_query and transactions_only_query, and with split_dataset elsewhere. When the request dataset is `errors`, _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns True, so the transactions-only discover query also gets count() rewritten to upsampled_count(). That result feeds has_transactions and therefore the split decision. scoped_dataset is accepted by _get_event_stats but never used for this check.

findings.title: Reads an option that this change does not register
findings.body: options.get('issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist', []) is called here, but the diff does not register this key in sentry/options defaults. Sentry's options manager raises for unregistered keys. This call runs on every cache miss for any events-stats timeseries request, before the dataset check. If the option is not registered elsewhere, those requests fail. The endpoint and unit tests mock sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options, so they cannot catch this. Confirm the registration exists or add it.

findings.title: Rewritten column uses an alias suffix that the field grammar does not accept
findings.body: The rewrite produces the literal string 'upsampled_count() as count'. Sentry's field grammar takes function(args) with nothing after the closing paren, so this string will not match the function form and will be treated as an unknown field or fail to parse. That turns affected requests into errors. The upsampled_count aggregate is only registered in DiscoverDatasetConfig (discover.py), yet _should_apply_sample_weight_transform also enables the rewrite for the `errors` dataset. Nothing in the diff shows this resolves through the errors query builder.

findings.title: sum(sample_weight) silently undercounts events that have no weight
findings.body: The docstring says the schema guarantees sample_weight for all events in allowlisted projects, so no null checks are needed. Nothing enforces that: the allowlist is per project, not per event. An event whose SDK does not send contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate may have a NULL or zero sample_weight. sum() skips NULLs, so such events contribute 0 instead of 1 to the count, silently, in any allowlisted project with mixed traffic.

findings.title: Gate tests miss the negated and OR cases the substring check gets wrong
findings.body: The discover gate is tested only with a plain 'event.type:error' query and a plain 'event.type:transaction' query. It is not tested with '!event.type:error', with 'event.type:error OR event.type:transaction', or with the split-path query shapes. Those are exactly the inputs where the substring check gives the wrong answer, so the bug above would pass this suite.

findings.title: Endpoint tests skip topEvents, dashboard split, and mixed-row queries
findings.body: The new class covers only plain count() timeseries for an error query, an all-allowlisted and a partial-allowlist case, and a transaction-only query. Not covered: topEvents with upsampling (the top_events_timeseries branch rewrites columns too), the dashboardWidgetId split path (where the dataset-scope bug lives), dataset=errors routing, and queries that mix error and transaction rows. test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events checks only a transaction-only query, which never reaches the rewrite, so it does not exercise the case the gate exists to block. The upsampled_count aggregate is also not tested directly.

findings.title: upsampled_count is a public aggregate with no allowlist gate
findings.body: The new aggregate is registered without private=True, unlike the adjacent function in the same converter. Any discover or events query can therefore call upsampled_count() on any project. The allowlist check exists only in the count() rewrite, so users can request an upsampled value for non-allowlisted projects, where sample_weight is typically absent and the result is 0 or misleading. Gate it or mark it private.

findings.title: invalidate_upsampling_cache is dead code and the 60s staleness is unmitigated
findings.body: invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but nothing in this change calls it. The eligibility cache set at line 38 has a 60 second TTL and is keyed only by org and project set. Removing a project from the allowlist therefore keeps upsampling it for up to a minute. The docstring says the function 'should be called when the allowlist configuration changes', but no call site exists.

findings.title: Docstrings contradict each other and the performance rationale is unsupported
findings.body: The function docstring (lines 23-25) says the 60 second cache avoids expensive repeated option lookups. The NOTE in _are_all_projects_error_upsampled (lines 50-53) says the allowlist is read fresh on every call and that this is intentional. The cache at lines 30-38 contradicts the second claim. The performance rationale is asserted without measurement, and the cache adds its own round trip on every request.

findings.title: Comments claim caching and consistency that the code does not provide
findings.body: The comments say 'this cached result ensures consistent behavior across query execution' and describe a performance optimization. Nothing is cached in this function. The eligibility is recomputed on every _get_event_stats call, which can be up to four times per request in the split path. The transform is also applied in three separate places (lines 232-233, 276-277, 295-296). The comments mislead the next maintainer about what is cached and why.

findings.title: Equations and orderby still use the unweighted count()
findings.body: The rewrite is applied only to the timeseries columns. Equations from get_equation_list (line 256 in the top-events branch, and in the RPC branch) and the orderby still refer to raw count(). A request mixing count() with an equation over count() returns a weighted count column next to an unweighted equation, which is inconsistent within one response.

findings.title: Unrelated change to a public API error message
findings.body: The topEvents validation message changes from 'If topEvents needs to be at least 1' to 'topEvents needs to be at least 1'. This is a wording change to a public API response that the PR description does not mention and that no test update in this diff accompanies. Clients or tests matching the old string will break.

findings.title: Bare except swallows errors and the helper changes every store_event call
findings.body: _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling wraps both the lookup and the float conversion in bare 'except Exception: pass'. A malformed contexts value is silently dropped, and the test sees no sample rate with no signal. The helper is invoked unconditionally from store_event (line 1049), so it affects every test that stores an event, not just the upsampling tests. Narrow the exception handling and make the side effect explicit.

findings.title: toInt64 truncates a float sum and can undercount by one
findings.body: sample_weight is a non-integer float (1/sample_rate), and toInt64 truncates toward zero. A float sum that lands just below an integer, for example 9.9999999999, becomes 9. Round before casting, e.g. round(sum(...)), so the integer result is not systematically low.

findings.title: Stray submodule-pointer file committed to the repository
findings.body: The PR adds a file named 'sentry-repo' whose only content is 'Subproject commit a5d29095...'. This looks like a submodule pointer written as a plain file, with no .gitmodules entry. It adds a meaningless file to the tree and looks like a leftover from a local submodule operation. It should be dropped from the PR.
